headline: Sensex and Nifty fall as RBI hikes repo rate to 5.5% and adopts calibrated tightening stance

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: The RBI Monetary Policy Committee hiked the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra shifted the policy stance to 'calibrated tightening' and ruled out near-term rate cuts
The Indian Rupee fell 22 paise to 96.57 against the U.S. dollar following the rate increase
Surging crude oil prices weighed on investor sentiment and contributed to the market decline
whatHappening: Sensex crashed over 500 points in early trade while Nifty dropped below the 22,600 level
Titan and Shriram Finance emerged as the top losers during the market session
GE Aerospace delivered four F404-IN20 engines to HAL for the Tejas LCA Mk 1A program
Markets trimmed some losses later in the day after the initial reaction to the RBI policy announcement
summary: Indian markets declined today as the RBI hiked the repo rate to 5.5% and adopted a 'calibrated tightening' stance. The Sensex fell over 500 points amid a weakening rupee and rising crude oil prices, though indices later trimmed some losses. Titan and Shriram Finance were the primary laggards, while HAL remained in focus due to engine deliveries from GE Aerospace.
